title: Can a very long thin rectangle be drawn the same way?
description: A rectangle with sides ten centimetres and two centimetres is drawn from one long side and two perpendiculars. The long thin drawing is checked for both properties of a rectangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same steps draw any rectangle, however long and thin, because the perpendiculars fix the angles and the marked lengths fix the sides. Watch for students who think a very thin figure is no longer a rectangle.

video_script.why: A learner draws a long thin rectangle from two side lengths and checks both properties of a rectangle.
video_script.substitution: the same way as the example in your book: a base, a perpendicular at each end, then the top joined across
video_script.anchor: a long thin rectangle being drawn on the board from a base and two upright lines
video_script.payoff_line: This long thin figure is still a rectangle.

final_answer.value: Rectangle PQRS with PQ = SR = 10 cm, PS = QR = 2 cm, all angles 90°. Both properties hold

maths_rules: perpendiculars at P and Q, with PS = 2 cm and QR = 2 cm
SR joined; SR = 10 cm = PQ and PS = QR = 2 cm, so opposite sides are equal
angle P = angle Q = angle R = angle S = 90°
video_script.design: A long thin rectangle is drawn in the same fixed order as before, then the two properties are checked on the finished drawing.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is another question from your book about drawing a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Its sides are ten centimetres and two centimetres, so it will be long and thin.
Will the long thin figure still be a rectangle?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='props'/>A rectangle has two properties, and its shape does not change them.
The first property is that opposite sides are equal in length.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second property is that all the angles are right angles.
<bookmark mark='plan'/>We draw it as before, with one side and a perpendicular at each end.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rectangle with sides ten centimetres and two centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: draw the rectangle PQRS and check both properties

marks.find: the task is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to draw it, and check both properties.

marks.pq: the base PQ is drawn and labelled 10 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='pq'/>Step one, draw pee queue equal to ten centimetres with the ruler.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: draw a perpendicular at P and at Q; mark S with PS = 2 cm and R with QR = 2 cm

marks.perps: the two perpendiculars rise from P and Q
marks.marks: S is marked 2 cm up the line at P
marks.markr: R is marked 2 cm up the line at Q

narration: <bookmark mark='perps'/>Step two, draw a perpendicular at pee and another at queue.
<bookmark mark='marks'/>On the one at pee, mark ess so that pee ess is two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='markr'/>On the one at queue, mark are so that queue are is two centimetres.

marks.join: the top side SR is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step three, join ess and are to finish the long thin figure.

beats.on_screen: Check: SR = 10 cm = PQ, PS = QR = 2 cm; every corner fits the set square at 90°

marks.sides: the equal opposite sides are marked with matching ticks
marks.angles: the four right-angle marks light up

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Check, ess are measures ten centimetres, the same as pee queue, and queue are matches pee ess.
<bookmark mark='angles'/>Each corner fits the set square at ninety degrees.

beats.on_screen: Answer: rectangle PQRS, PQ = SR = 10 cm, PS = QR = 2 cm, all angles 90°. Both properties hold

marks.res: the rectangle glows with its sides labelled

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>This long thin figure is still a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Its opposite sides are ten centimetres and two centimetres, and every angle is ninety degrees.
